page: Microsoft Azure F4as_v6 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on AMD EPYC 9V74 processors operating at 3.7 GHz. The system provides 4 dedicated physical x86_64 cores without simultaneous multithreading, mapped directly to 4 vCPUs. Cache allocation includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 vector support with VNNI and BF16, alongside AES and SHA cryptographic accelerations. The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of memory, yielding 4.0 GB per vCPU, without bundled local storage or included public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread execution metrics. The dedicated AMD EPYC cores deliver upper-quartile scores in stress-ng single-core compute and Geekbench single-core evaluations, including high performance in text processing workloads. Multi-threaded evaluations, including multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench runs, reflect standard mid-tier throughput consistent with a 4-core layout. Synthetic memory benchmarks show normal cached bandwidth at 590.47 GB/sec for small blocks, whereas large uncached read transfers fall into lower performance bands at 37.88 GB/sec.

Without included ephemeral disks or discrete GPU accelerators, the instance relies on remote network storage for persistence. The absence of hyperthreading overhead provides predictable per-core execution, making the F4as_v6 resource-efficient for CPU-bound tasks that prioritize single-thread throughput over aggregate parallel density. Tradeoffs include modest memory throughput on large streaming working sets and limited capacity for large-scale local AI inference.

The hardware configuration suits web application serving, batch data processing, continuous integration compilation tasks, and Redis caching tiers where dedicated CPU scheduling and high per-core performance are critical.
description: Microsoft Azure F4as_v6 is a compute-oriented virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. Utilizing an x86_64 architecture with one thread per core and 32 MB of L3 cache, it delivers 16.0 GB of system memory at a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance does not include bundled local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators. Benchmark profiles highlight strong single-core CPU throughput and text processing efficiency, paired with standard multi-threaded performance and mid-range cached memory bandwidth. Uncached sequential memory read speeds remain a limiting factor during large data transfers. Given its dedicated core execution and support for AVX-512 extensions, the instance is effective for CPU-intensive web servers, application build pipelines, microservices, and general compute workloads requiring consistent instruction rates without hyperthreading contention.
